svg.aria-label: The write-ahead log and what reads it: every change goes to WAL before the data page; crash recovery replays it, the archiver copies segments for point-in-time recovery, standbys stream and replay it, and logical replication decodes it into row changes

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Every change is written to WAL before the data page. Recovery, backups and both replication types all read it.

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: write-ahead rule: log first, page later

svg.text: wal_level = logical. WAL is decoded into row changes:

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: PUBLICATION on the source, SUBSCRIPTION on the target.

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Not replicated: DDL, sequence values, large objects.

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Streaming replication copies bytes of the whole cluster. Logical replication is selective and works across major versions,

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: which is why it can cut a major-version upgrade's downtime to the seconds of the cutover.

text.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Source: PostgreSQL Course 07, Chapters 1-4 (WAL, checkpoints, archiving and PITR, streaming and logical replication).
